input: Write a due diligence memo on Databricks

business.claim: Databricks calls itself 'the Data and AI company.' It is headquartered in San Francisco and has 30+ offices worldwide.

Its products include Lakehouse (data warehousing), Lakebase (a serverless Postgres database for AI agents), Genie (an 'AI coworker' or business agent) and Unity AI Gateway (governance and cost control across multiple AI models).
It sells to enterprises: more than 20,000 organizations, including 70% of the Fortune 500 (company claim).

Customers pay by consumption, priced per DBU (Databricks Unit) against committed spend (DBCU commits). Photon and Serverless SKUs carry higher per-DBU rates. This comes from a third-party procurement advisory paper.

It is expanding into cybersecurity. In June 2026 it agreed to buy Panther Labs, an AI SOC platform, for an undisclosed price. This is its third security acquisition and puts it up against CrowdStrike and Cisco's Splunk.
Founded in 2013. It helps companies build AI agents and apps on their own data.

traction.claim: Company claim: more than 1,000 customers at a run-rate above $1M and more than 100 above $10M. This is up from >800 and >70 in February 2026.
Company claim: net revenue retention above 140%. The AI products had passed a $1.4B revenue run-rate.
Company claim: Lakehouse (data warehousing) run-rate is above $1.5B and growing more than 100% year over year. Lakebase run-rate is above $100M.
Named customers (company claim): adidas, AT&T, Bayer, Block, Mastercard, Rivian, Unilever.
Microsoft took part as an equity investor in the round that closed in February 2026 (company claim).
Ranked No. 3 on CNBC's 2026 Disruptor 50 list. CNBC says Databricks has passed Snowflake in market value.

team.claim: Ali Ghodsi is co-founder and CEO.
Matei Zaharia is CTO. Analysts named him and Ghodsi as the people the company would rely on for AI leadership after Naveen Rao left.

Executives as listed by an aggregator: David Conte (CFO since Oct 2019), Ion Stoica (co-founder and Executive Chair), Hatim Shafique (COO), Rick Schultz (CMO), Ron Gabrisko (CRO), Andy Kofoid (President, Global Field Operations), Reynold Xin (Chief Architect), Naveen Zutshi (CIO), Fermín Serna (CSO), Amy Reichanadter (Chief People Officer). Co-founders Patrick Wendell, Arsalan Tavakoli-Shiraji and Andy Konwinski are also listed. Data is as of August 2026 and not company-verified.
Notable departure: Naveen Rao, head of AI and co-founder of MosaicML (bought by Databricks in 2023), left. Moor Insights flagged a risk that innovation slows until leadership stabilizes.

funding.claim: Prior rounds: $10B at a $62B valuation in December 2024, then $1B at a $100B valuation in September 2025.
Series L announced at more than $4B and a $134B valuation. Named investors were Insight Partners, Fidelity Management & Research and J.P. Morgan Asset Management.

Series L completed: about $5B equity at a $134B valuation plus about $2B in new debt capacity, for more than $7B in total. Equity investors included JPMorganChase, Glade Brook, Goldman Sachs Alternatives, Microsoft, Morgan Stanley, Neuberger, QIA and UBS funds. JPMorgan Chase Bank led the credit facilities.
Term sheet signed at a $188B valuation, led by Coatue, with the amount not disclosed. TechCrunch notes other outlets reported about $3B, citing the WSJ.

Latest round and last known valuation: $5B strategic round at $190B, led by Coatue. Participants included Blackstone, MGX, T. Rowe Price-advised accounts, Sixth Street Growth, BOND, Clearlake, Point72, Premji Invest and TPG, plus existing investors such as a16z, Thrive, GIC, Temasek and NEA.
Still private. The CEO says Databricks intends to go public but cites 'too much distraction in the public market' right now.

financial_signals.claim: Company-reported revenue run-rate above $4.8B in fiscal Q3, growing more than 55% year over year.
Company-reported revenue run-rate above $5.4B in fiscal Q4, growing more than 65% year over year, with positive free cash flow over the trailing 12 months.
Company-reported revenue run-rate above $7B in fiscal Q2, growing more than 80% year over year, with positive adjusted free cash flow over the trailing 12 months. No audited figures are public.

Headcount trend (aggregator, observed LinkedIn-style profiles rather than a company total): 12,299 in August 2025 rose to 14,237 in July 2026, up 15.8%, with 2,822 observed hires in the last 12 months.

Hiring and layoffs, from a recruiting-firm blog (KORE1, which has a disclosed conflict and some internal date and round errors): no WARN filing or company-wide layoff found. The blog estimates fewer than 50 targeted cuts in March 2026, from anonymous posts, and counted more than 840 open requisitions in early May 2026.

legal_and_regulatory.claim: In re Mosaic LLM Litigation (N.D. Cal., Judge Charles Breyer): authors' copyright class action against Databricks and MosaicML over training LLMs (including DBRX) on books. The motion to dismiss the Second Amended Complaint was denied on 2026-04-22. Summary judgment motions on infringement and fair use were filed on 2026-06-30, and the SJ/Daubert hearing moved to 2026-12-18. Source is a blog that tracks the docket.
Mealey's: the judge ruled that Mosaic and Databricks will face direct copyright infringement claims, finding plaintiffs adequately tied the copying of their works to LLM training.

Poulin Holdings, LLC v. Databricks, Inc., No. 4:26-cv-00245 (E.D. Tex., Judge Jeremy Kernodle): patent infringement complaint filed 2026-03-10 over the '977 and '090 patents. Status is not shown. Source is a docket aggregator.
No data breach, regulatory action or sanctions matter was found in the searches. No regulator or court page confirming this was opened.

reputation.claim: Critical press: TechCrunch called it unusual to announce the $188B round before the money was in hand. It credited part of the valuation jump to an 'AI halo' and noted the 'run out of letters' meme about Databricks' many rounds.

Pattern of customer cost complaints, from a procurement advisory with a commercial interest: committing to vendor usage forecasts, renewal commits that open 25–60% higher, Photon and Serverless premiums, always-on AI endpoints, and retirement of the Azure Standard tier.
After Rao's exit, analyst Robert Kramer (Moor Insights) warned that rivals could use the AI leadership gap to win customers. Futurum's Bradley Shimmin disagreed.

red_flags.claim: Active AI copyright class action in which direct infringement claims survived dismissal. The summary judgment and fair-use hearing is set for 2026-12-18, so the damages exposure is not yet known.
The valuation rose from $134B to $190B in about six months. The July round was announced before it closed and without a disclosed size.
Every financial metric is a self-reported run-rate. Free cash flow is described as 'adjusted', and there are no audited financials or an S-1. The CEO is deferring an IPO.
The head of AI (MosaicML co-founder Naveen Rao) left in September 2025.
Pending patent infringement suit in E.D. Texas (Poulin Holdings).

output.verdict: Strong: company-reported growth is speeding up, with run-rate climbing from $4.8B to above $7B and growth rising from 55% to over 80% year over year between Dec 2025 and Aug 2026. The company also reports net retention above 140%, more than 1,000 customers at $1M+, positive (adjusted) free cash flow and a large group of top-tier investors. Needs a closer look: none of the financials are audited and the $190B valuation assumes growth continues. The MosaicML/DBRX copyright case reaches summary judgment on 2026-12-18, a patent suit is pending, and there are customer cost complaints and execution risk from moving into AI agents and security through acquisitions.
